Aspects

Source: DESIGN-ASPECTS.md, reconciled with DESIGN-WORLD.md, DESIGN-HOOK-CONFLICT.md, and DESIGN-HOOK-RESOLUTION.md. Status: implemented. All six identities are wired into Assets/Scripts/Core/Combat/CombatSimulation.cs and confirmed in this repo's current code and content (verified independently while writing this page, not just trusted from the doc).

Originally an Aspect was only a colour and a damage multiplier (AspectChart.Multiplier, ×1.20 / ×0.85) read by almost nothing else in the codebase. Each aspect now owns one real rule in the combat effect pipeline, chosen from what the existing hero kits were already doing rather than invented fresh. The old matchup-wheel multiplier still exists as a secondary layer, narrowed to ×1.10 / ×0.92 (see "The matchup wheel" below) so it doesn't out-argue the new identities.

Ember — escalates

Belief: nothing changes without destruction.

Mechanic: Burn instances from Ember sources stack as separate entries instead of overwriting each other — a second Ember application deepens the existing fire rather than replacing it. Ember buys damage that lands later, on the victim's own turn. Hook: CombatUnit.AddOrRefresh.

Fit: Kalyx Emberwright's Cinder Bloom (AllEnemies damage + Burn) is clean Ember. His old passive Kindling (+30% damage vs. burning targets) was a flat percentage bonus, exactly what the design rule bans — it has been cut from heroes.json.

Status: implemented and content-clean — Kindling is gone.

Tide — redirects

Belief: nothing should remain fixed.

Mechanic: energy never gets discarded. Overflow past EnergyMax is handed to the living ally furthest from casting instead of being thrown away. Hook: Sim.AddEnergy, keyed on the granter (a unit's own basic-attack/on-damage regen doesn't redirect — only energy explicitly granted by a living Tide unit does).

Fit: Maeve Corrin fits completely — Tidal Cadence and Rising Chorus are already about other people's cast timing, and she's the hero who most obviously wastes the old clamped system.

Status: implemented. The competing relic Tidewrought Metronome (which wanted the same clamp) was cut outright, not relocated — see Open Questions and DESIGN-HOOK-RESOLUTION.md.

Verdant — persists

Belief: what survives deserves to continue.

Mechanic: healing/warding with nowhere to go banks forward as a Regen status instead of being clamped away. Hook: Sim.ApplyHealValue's early return on missing <= 0.

Fit: Wren Ilyra's Verdant Tide (heal AllAllies) is Verdant, but two of her three kit pieces aren't: the Cleanse on the same ability is anti-Umbra, and Rootbound (a Shield at battle start) is Lumen's rule. She reads as a healer with a protection kit stapled on.

Status: implemented. The competing relic Green Hour Vessel was also cut, for the same reason as Metronome — the Shield effect handler was found to have no discard to intercept at all, so there was nowhere to relocate it to.

Gale — disrupts sequencing

Belief: nothing should be held in place.

Mechanic: Gale manipulates initiative directly. A Gale unit that lands a kill re-enters the current round's turn order; Gale's Slow pushes a target later within the same round rather than just the next one. Hook: Sim.TurnOrder()/Execute's turn loop, and the existing PassiveTrigger.OnKill call site in DealRawDamage's death branch (which nothing used before this).

Fit: Ryn Solvarr's targeting (LowestHpEnemy on both attacks) is perfect Gale-as-finisher, but her old passive Follow-Through triggered OnCriticalHit and granted flat energy — a Tide-shaped passive on a Gale hero, the clearest cross-wiring in the roster. Fixed: the trigger is now OnKill. (The effect itself is still EnergyGain, Tide's verb — the doc notes this only partially un-cross-wires her.)

Status: implemented, with a guard: a re-entering Gale unit could otherwise shed its own statuses at double rate, so status expiry is now once-per-round-per-carrier rather than once-per-turn. Also capped per unit per round (galeExtraTurnsPerRound) to stop a single Gale unit from resolving an entire round unilaterally at team size 5 — measured and confirmed necessary during implementation. At team size 3 this was safe without a cap; at 5 it required one.

Umbra — removes and conceals

Belief: not everything should be known.

Mechanic: harmful statuses applied by an Umbra source cannot be cleansed. (An earlier version also made them not tick down while the applier lived — DESIGN-WORLD judged that half wrong, since "doesn't expire" is persistence, which is Verdant's word, not Umbra's. That clause was cut; only uncleansable survived.) Hook: Sim.ExpireStatuses, the Cleanse branch of ApplyEffect, AddOrRefresh.

Fit: Nyx Serrow fits well — she targets HighestAttackEnemy and applies uncleansable DefenseDown. One stray: her Focus self-buff on Umbral Step is a crit-chance bonus, which is Gale's axis, not Umbra's — left as-is, noted as the one line of her kit that would logically move.

Status: implemented (uncleansable-only version). Weakens at team size 5 — see Combat Systems and Open Questions for the still-undecided team-size-5 dilution question.

Lumen — marks and defines

Belief: everything should have a knowable place.

Mechanic: originally specified as "Lumen intercepts" (absorption-first). DESIGN-WORLD re-weighted this: the actual identity is that a living Lumen unit answers every single-enemy targeting question aimed at its side — it outranks even a non-Lumen ally's Taunt. Absorption is just what happens once you're always the answer, not a separate rule. Hook: Sim.ResolveTargets' FindTaunter override (renamed FindTargetAnchor), which needed no new code for the absorption half — the Shield-absorb block in DealRawDamage already worked unconditionally.

Fit: Orrin Kaal was originally labelled Ember with a kit of Shield/Taunt/DefenseUp — the Lumen rule three times over. He has been relabelled from "aspect": "Ember" to "aspect": "Lumen" in heroes.json (confirmed in the current content file) — a one-string content change, kit untouched. This activated the Lumen↔Umbra matchup pair for the first time in the game (previously inert with zero Lumen units). A predicted difficulty spike on the Umbra-heavy tutorial stage was measured and did not appear — the stage actually got easier, because Orrin's routing benefit (enemy hits anchor onto him) outweighed the multiplier penalty.

Status: implemented, built last as planned (it was considered the least-trustworthy identity, derived by elimination rather than read off an existing kit). Orrin is currently the only Lumen unit in the game on either side.

The matchup wheel

Kept as a secondary layer rather than replaced (replacing it would have deleted shipped work across three files). Narrowed from ×1.20/×0.85 to ×1.10/×0.92 so the six new identities aren't drowned out by a single colour-vs-colour roll. One coupled constant had to move with it: Debrief.AspectFactorThreshold (was 1.2, which would have silently stopped the results-screen "you were the wrong colour" clause from ever firing again at the new 1.10 multiplier).

Roster fit summary

Per DESIGN-ASPECTS section 3: of the six starting/roster heroes, only Maeve (Tide) was a clean fit from the start. Two were near-fits with one stray line (Nyx, Kalyx). Three needed a relabel or a passive fix (Orrin relabelled to Lumen, Ryn's passive trigger fixed, Wren still split across Verdant/anti-Umbra/Lumen with no plan to un-split her). See Heroes for the per-hero detail and current kit data.
